title: Too many turkeys: how we prompted our Thanksgiving games 🦃
author: gameover_com
selftext:
Our study of the [70 Halloween browser mini games](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/what-ai-thinks-halloween-notes-from-70-spooky-games-gameover-com-cmbic/) developed with AI found that most games were common mechanics with Halloween skin, not a deep exploration of Halloween themes.



For Thanksgiving, we used Claude Opus 5.5 to reskin 39 Halloween games. The batch came out festive and too familiar:

\- Tom the turkey was in about 25 of the 39 games.

\- Most were set on a farm or in a kitchen at golden hour, with gingham, one font and one banjo tune.

\- Pies, gravy and cranberries were most of the objects. Family, friends, travel and autumn were missing.



Disappointed in the selection, we prompted for another batch that probed deeper: family, friends, autumn and other Thanksgiving traditions. Claude reviewed the games then decided on what to select, update, rebuild or build new according to these rules:

\- The mechanic comes from a tradition or a feeling, and the holiday is in what you do.

\- 12 genres and 12 settings, with a different palette, font and music bed for each.

\- A turkey only where it belongs. Turkey Bowl is the name of the backyard football game.



Four of the 12 are new, four were rebuilt, two reworked and two polished. A rework keeps the engine and level data and moves the theme into the rules. A rebuild reuses the source's tech and changes the core loop. Some of what that produced:

\- Food Drive is Pantry Jam reworked, with the sliding puzzle now moving donation crates to delivery vans.

\- House Rules is Cranberry Chain reworked into a versus puzzle at a family game night.

\- Over the River is Hayride Highway rebuilt. The road renderer stayed, and a backseat of kids asking if we're there yet arrived.

\- Leaf Day is new. You rake the yard and pick the moment the kid cannonballs into the pile.

\- Turkey Bowl is new. Your throw goes to a cousin while the dog chases the ball and Grandpa referees from a lawn chair.

\- Flyway is new. The tired lead goose rotates to the back of the V.

\- Seating Chart is new. Every relative needs a seat that makes them happy, and the whole table raises a glass when the last card goes down.



What changed between the batches:

\- In the second batch, we named a goal and some themes, and got a diagnosis and a plan.

\- Giving Claude the choice between polishing, reworking, rebuilding and building new led to 4 new games.



Happy Thanksgiving and enjoy the mini games at [https://gameover.com/gallery?q=turkey](https://gameover.com/gallery?q=turkey)
